description: Grafana replica of the Copernicus CAMS Fire Emissions Watch, built on the kepler.gl panel and reading ECMWF's public Parquet store live with DuckDB.

panels.description: Hides the weakest fires everywhere at once. The ranking and the stats drop the cell-days in SQL; **the maps keep their full dataset and apply the same threshold as a kepler range filter**, so dragging the slider re-masks them instantly, with no query. Units follow the Variable picker: MW for frpfire, t/day for cfire. The daily global chart is the one panel it cannot touch — CAMS precomputes that series, there are no cells to filter.
panels.title: Minimum cell value — drag to hide the weakest fires

panels.description: What the map is showing right now. Draw a polygon with the map's draw tool and it takes over; delete it and the viewport is back.

targets.rawSql:
WITH px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
                     -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat,
                     lon_idx, lat_idx, value, region_idx
              FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])
              -- Slider threshold. Panels that aggregate drop the cell-day here, in
              -- SQL. The maps do NOT: they load the whole dataset and get the
              -- same threshold as a kepler range filter, so dragging the
              -- slider re-masks them in the browser without re-querying.
              WHERE ($minval = '' OR value >= CAST($minval AS INTEGER))),
zone AS (SELECT CASE WHEN $area = '' THEN NULL ELSE ST_GeomFromText($area) END AS g)
SELECT count(DISTINCT CAST(p.lon_idx AS BIGINT)*10000 + p.lat_idx) AS "Active Fires and Hotspots",
       count(DISTINCT p.dt)                          AS "Days with fire"
FROM px p CROSS JOIN zone
WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt) AND (CASE WHEN zone.g IS NULL
                THEN p.lon BETWEEN $west AND $east AND p.lat BETWEEN $south AND $north
                ELSE ST_Within(ST_Point(p.lon, p.lat), zone.g) END)

panels.description: Every polygon is one cell of the GFAS grid, summed over the dashboard time range. Pan or zoom and watch the panels beside it follow. Draw a polygon with the map's draw tool and the polygon takes over from the viewport; delete it and the viewport is back. Pick a country in the ranking beside it and the Country tab opens, framed on that country and outlining its subdivisions — this map stays global.

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
reg AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
countries AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country, admin0_continent[i] AS continente
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
                     -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat,
                     lon_idx, lat_idx, value, region_idx
              FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}]))
SELECT ST_AsHEXWKB(ST_MakeEnvelope(p.lon-0.05, p.lat-0.05, p.lon+0.05, p.lat+0.05)) AS geom,
       round(CAST(sum(p.value) AS DOUBLE), 1)  AS value,
       count(*)                AS ndays,
       any_value(c.country)       AS country
FROM px p
LEFT JOIN reg r ON r.region_idx = p.region_idx
LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.iso3 = r.iso3
WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt)
GROUP BY p.lon, p.lat

-- El humo, la capa que el visor de CAMS dibuja y esta réplica no tenía.
--
-- No trae filas de datos: nombra un store Zarr y una variable de él, y el panel
-- se las pide al servidor de teselas. `omaod550` es el espesor óptico de los
-- aerosoles de materia orgánica a 550 nm — el humo — y es la variable que el
-- visor pinta.
--
-- El token viaja en la URL a propósito: es el mismo que ECMWF publica dentro
-- del bundle de su propio visor, no un secreto de nadie.
--
-- El store es una ventana rodante —dos pasadas al día, unos tres meses— y la
-- última es la de ayer. Fuera de ese rango cada tesela contestaría 500, así que
-- las fechas se recortan aquí en vez de dejar que lo descubra el mapa.
--
-- Una sola fila, sin columna `time`: la escena del último día de la ventana del
-- dashboard. Sin fecha no hay reloj propio del mapa —el widget de kepler ocupa
-- un tercio del panel— y el humo sigue igualmente al selector de tiempo de
-- arriba, porque la fecha sale de él. Los dos ejes del store, que es 4-D, van
-- juntos en `zarr_sel`.
SELECT 'https://arco.datastores.ecmwf.int/cadl-arco-time-001/arco/cams_global_atmospheric_composition_forecasts/sfc-multiforecast/timeChunked.zarr?_fet=fire-watch-827a2651-8e26-4bc1-ac44-9351fcb916af' AS zarr_url,
       'omaod550' AS zarr_variable,
       'time=' || strftime(dia, '%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00.000000000') || ',time_step=0' AS zarr_sel
FROM (SELECT least($__timeTo()::DATE, current_date - 1) AS dia)

panels.description: Only the regions that fall inside what the map is showing: the drawn polygon if there is one, the viewport otherwise. **Magnitude and intensity are the contribution inside that zone**, as daily values over the dashboard time range — units for cfire: kt C and kg C/km²; for frpfire: GW and W/km² (intensity divides by the country's full area). **The anomaly σ is not**: it is the whole-country figure CAMS publishes for the $win window, because recomputing the 2003–2025 baseline inside a polygon takes 44 s. Zoomed out, with the default 7-day range, magnitude and intensity match the original viewer exactly.

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
reg AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
countries AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country, admin0_continent[i] AS continente
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
                     -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat,
                     lon_idx, lat_idx, value, region_idx
              FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])
              -- Slider threshold. Panels that aggregate drop the cell-day here, in
              -- SQL. The maps do NOT: they load the whole dataset and get the
              -- same threshold as a kepler range filter, so dragging the
              -- slider re-masks them in the browser without re-querying.
              WHERE ($minval = '' OR value >= CAST($minval AS INTEGER))),
zone AS (SELECT CASE WHEN $area = '' THEN NULL ELSE ST_GeomFromText($area) END AS g),
areas AS (SELECT * FROM (SELECT adm0 AS iso3, area_sq_km FROM read_parquet('https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/data/countries_admin0_v2gisco_z0.parquet'))),
d AS (SELECT c.iso3 AS iso3, c.country AS country, p.dt AS dt, sum(p.value) AS v
          FROM px p
          CROSS JOIN zone
          JOIN reg r ON r.region_idx = p.region_idx
          JOIN countries c ON c.iso3 = r.iso3
          WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt) AND (CASE WHEN zone.g IS NULL
                THEN p.lon BETWEEN $west AND $east AND p.lat BETWEEN $south AND $north
                ELSE ST_Within(ST_Point(p.lon, p.lat), zone.g) END)
          GROUP BY 1, 2, 3),
bounds AS (SELECT min(dt) AS d0, max(dt) AS d1 FROM d),
ndays AS (SELECT date_diff('day', d0, d1) + 1 AS n FROM bounds),
top AS (SELECT d.iso3 AS iso3, d.country AS country, sum(d.v) AS total
        FROM d
        JOIN areas a ON a.iso3 = d.iso3
        GROUP BY 1, 2
        ORDER BY total DESC
        LIMIT ${topn:raw})
-- Rejilla densa país × día, y el valor a DOUBLE: sum() sobre INT32 da HUGEINT,
-- que el driver entrega como string. Sin las dos cosas el frame vuelve en
-- formato largo, timeSeriesTable no lo convierte y la sparkline desaparece.
, days AS (SELECT unnest(range(CAST((SELECT d0 FROM bounds) AS DATE),
                              CAST((SELECT d1 FROM bounds) AS DATE) + INTERVAL 1 DAY,
                              INTERVAL 1 DAY))::DATE AS dt)
SELECT g.dt AS "time", g.country AS country,
       CAST(COALESCE(d.v, 0) AS DOUBLE) AS value
FROM (SELECT top.iso3 AS iso3, top.country AS country, days.dt AS dt FROM top CROSS JOIN days) g
LEFT JOIN d ON d.iso3 = g.iso3 AND d.dt = g.dt
ORDER BY 1

WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
reg AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
countries AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country, admin0_continent[i] AS continente
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
                     -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat,
                     lon_idx, lat_idx, value, region_idx
              FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])
              -- Slider threshold. Panels that aggregate drop the cell-day here, in
              -- SQL. The maps do NOT: they load the whole dataset and get the
              -- same threshold as a kepler range filter, so dragging the
              -- slider re-masks them in the browser without re-querying.
              WHERE ($minval = '' OR value >= CAST($minval AS INTEGER))),
zone AS (SELECT CASE WHEN $area = '' THEN NULL ELSE ST_GeomFromText($area) END AS g),
areas AS (SELECT * FROM (SELECT adm0 AS iso3, area_sq_km FROM read_parquet('https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/data/countries_admin0_v2gisco_z0.parquet'))),
d AS (SELECT c.iso3 AS iso3, c.country AS country, p.dt AS dt, sum(p.value) AS v,
             avg(p.lat) AS lat, avg(p.lon) AS lon
          FROM px p
          CROSS JOIN zone
          JOIN reg r ON r.region_idx = p.region_idx
          JOIN countries c ON c.iso3 = r.iso3
          WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt) AND (CASE WHEN zone.g IS NULL
                THEN p.lon BETWEEN $west AND $east AND p.lat BETWEEN $south AND $north
                ELSE ST_Within(ST_Point(p.lon, p.lat), zone.g) END)
          GROUP BY 1, 2, 3),
bounds AS (SELECT min(dt) AS d0, max(dt) AS d1 FROM d),
ndays AS (SELECT date_diff('day', d0, d1) + 1 AS n FROM bounds),
top AS (SELECT d.iso3 AS iso3, d.country AS country, sum(d.v) AS total,
               avg(d.lat) AS clat, avg(d.lon) AS clon
        FROM d
        JOIN areas a ON a.iso3 = d.iso3
        GROUP BY 1, 2
        ORDER BY total DESC
        LIMIT ${topn:raw}),
s AS (SELECT unnest(map_entries(windows['${win:raw}']['admin0'])) AS e
      FROM read_json('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/latest/${var:raw}/summary.json.gz',
        columns = {'dataset_day':'VARCHAR','variable':'VARCHAR',
                   'windows':'MAP(VARCHAR, MAP(VARCHAR, MAP(VARCHAR, DOUBLE[])))'})),
trend AS (SELECT d.iso3 AS iso3,
                avg(CASE WHEN d.dt >  l.d1 - INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN d.v END) AS fin,
                avg(CASE WHEN d.dt <  l.d0 + INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN d.v END) AS ini
         FROM d CROSS JOIN bounds l GROUP BY 1)
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY top.total DESC)  AS rank,
       top.country                                     AS country,
       CASE WHEN t.fin IS NULL OR t.ini IS NULL OR t.ini = 0 THEN 0
            WHEN t.fin > t.ini * 1.05 THEN  1
            WHEN t.fin < t.ini * 0.95 THEN -1
            ELSE 0 END                              AS arrow,
       -- Pixels come in MW (frpfire) and t/day (cfire); the summary comes in W and
       -- kg/day. Hence the factors here are not the summary's.
       round(top.total / n.n / 1e3, 2)                                     AS magnitude,
       round(top.total / n.n
             * CASE WHEN '${var:raw}' = 'cfire' THEN 1e3 ELSE 1e6 END
             / a.area_sq_km, 1)                                            AS intensity,
       round(s.e.value[4], 2)                                              AS anomaly,
       round(top.clat, 4)                                                  AS clat,
       round(top.clon, 4)                                                  AS clon
FROM top
CROSS JOIN ndays n
JOIN areas a ON a.iso3 = top.iso3
LEFT JOIN trend t ON t.iso3 = top.iso3
LEFT JOIN s ON s.e.key = top.iso3
ORDER BY top.total DESC

panels.description: World daily total against the mean of the same days of the year over 2003–2025. From the stats/daily.json.gz that CAMS precomputes.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (CAST(e.key AS INTEGER)) DAY AS d,
                  e.value[2]/1e9 AS v
           FROM (SELECT unnest(map_entries(m)) AS e FROM read_json('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/stats/${var:raw}/daily.json.gz', columns = {'m':'MAP(VARCHAR, DOUBLE[])'}, records = false) t(m))),
clim AS (SELECT strftime(d, '%m-%d') AS md, avg(v) AS mean
         FROM s
         WHERE d < date_trunc('year', CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP))
         GROUP BY 1)
SELECT s.d                    AS "time",
       round(s.v, 2)          AS "This year",
       round(c.mean, 2)      AS "Historical mean"
FROM s JOIN clim c ON c.md = strftime(s.d, '%m-%d')
WHERE $__timeFilter(s.d)
ORDER BY 1

options.content:
### Global wildfire emissions, tracked every day

Wildfire intensity and carbon emissions for every region — derived from satellite observations by
the CAMS Global Fire Assimilation System and compared against 23 years of history.

A Grafana replica of [CAMS Fire Emissions Watch](https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/),
built on the **Kepler Geospatial Maps** panel. Data is read **live** from ECMWF's public Parquet
store with DuckDB (`httpfs`): no ETL, no database, and — with one exception — no local copy.
That is why each panel takes 1–3 s to resolve.

The exception is the two country-history charts. CAMS publishes its per-country daily series as
Arrow IPC inside gzip, which DuckDB cannot read over HTTP, so `testdata/make-firedata.py`
converts it once into 8 MB of Parquet. Every other number on this page is fetched live.

**Global Fire Assimilation System.** GFAS assimilates fire radiative power (FRP) observations from
satellite-based sensors to produce daily estimates of biomass burning emissions, a consistent daily
record running from 2003 to yesterday. The FRP observations assimilated in the GFAS version 1.2
shown here are the NASA Terra MODIS and Aqua MODIS active fire products. Cells are 0.1° × 0.1°;
`frpfire` is fire radiative power, `cfire` is carbon emissions.

GFAS fire data is based on satellite observations of thermal anomalies at the surface, most commonly
associated with vegetation fires — but detections from other heat sources, such as active volcanoes
and gas flaring, and from reflective surfaces are also possible. GFAS tries to minimise these
spurious detections.

**Not replicated here:** the smoke layer. The original overlays organic matter aerosol optical depth
at 550 nm from the CAMS global forecasting system; that store sits behind an application token, so
it is out of scope here. It is free to download from the Atmosphere Data Store under the Copernicus
licence, as are all the datasets behind this dashboard.

**What this version does and the original does not:** the top map publishes its viewport, the
country you click and the polygon you draw, and the panels around it recompute on their own. There,
the map and the charts are islands.

---

*Generated using Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service information [2026]* — this dashboard
contains modified CAMS information. Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any
use of the data. Licensed under CC-BY-4.0.

*Disclaimer.* References to geographical or other territories and groupings are based on terms
provided to ECMWF by ECMWF Member States and Co-operating States, terminology used by other relevant
international organisations or other sources deemed relevant by ECMWF. Their use does not constitute
or imply an expression of opinion by ECMWF concerning the status of any State or territory, or its
frontiers or sovereignty. The colours, boundaries and names shown, and the designations used, are
not intended to imply any judgment, official endorsement or acceptance by ECMWF as to the legal
status or frontier of any territory.

panels.description: Only the selected country: its 0.1° cells over the dashboard time range, with its subdivisions outlined. The map fits itself to the data, so it frames whichever country you pick — from the dropdown above or by clicking a row in the global ranking.

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
reg AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
countries AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country, admin0_continent[i] AS continente
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
                     -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat,
                     lon_idx, lat_idx, value, region_idx
              FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}]))
SELECT ST_AsHEXWKB(ST_MakeEnvelope(p.lon-0.05, p.lat-0.05, p.lon+0.05, p.lat+0.05)) AS geom,
       round(CAST(sum(p.value) AS DOUBLE), 1)  AS value,
       count(*)                AS ndays,
       any_value(c.country)       AS country
FROM px p
LEFT JOIN reg r ON r.region_idx = p.region_idx
LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.iso3 = r.iso3
WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt)
  -- Vista de país: sin país elegido no devuelve nada, y la capa
  -- desaparece sola en vez de enseñar el mundo entero.
  AND $country_sel <> '' AND c.country = $country_sel
GROUP BY p.lon, p.lat

WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1[i] AS adm1, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
pick AS (SELECT max(iso3) AS iso3 FROM parent WHERE country = $country_sel),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt, value, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])),
agg AS (SELECT s.adm1 AS adm1, s.name AS name, sum(p.value) AS total
        FROM px p JOIN sub s ON s.region_idx = p.region_idx
        WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt)
        GROUP BY 1, 2),
-- Las geometrías vienen como listas anidadas GeoArrow, no como WKB: hay que
-- rearmar el WKT a mano. Los anillos no vienen cerrados, así que se cierran; y
-- ST_MakeValid deja un tercio como GEOMETRYCOLLECTION, que el decodificador del
-- plugin rechaza, de ahí el ST_CollectionExtract a polígonos.
geo AS (SELECT g.adm1 AS adm1,
               ST_CollectionExtract(ST_MakeValid(ST_GeomFromText(
                 'MULTIPOLYGON(' || list_aggregate(list_transform(g.geometry, poly ->
                     '(' || list_aggregate(list_transform(poly, ring ->
                         '(' || list_aggregate(list_transform(
                             CASE WHEN ring[1] = ring[len(ring)] THEN ring ELSE list_append(ring, ring[1]) END,
                             pt -> pt[1]::VARCHAR || ' ' || pt[2]::VARCHAR), 'string_agg', ', ') || ')'
                     ), 'string_agg', ', ') || ')'
                 ), 'string_agg', ', ') || ')')), 3) AS shape
        FROM read_parquet('https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/data/countries_admin1_v2gisco.parquet') g
        WHERE $country_sel <> '' AND g.adm0 = (SELECT iso3 FROM pick))
SELECT ST_AsHEXWKB(geo.shape)                    AS geom,
       COALESCE(agg.name, geo.adm1)              AS subdivision,
       round(CAST(COALESCE(agg.total, 0) AS DOUBLE) / 1e3, 2) AS total
FROM geo LEFT JOIN agg ON agg.adm1 = geo.adm1

panels.title: Where it burns in $country_sel

panels.description: Every year since 2003 as its own line, the climatological mean, and the year in progress. X axis is the day of the year, so the curves overlay. Read from testdata/fire/*.parquet — CAMS's own per-country series, converted once by testdata/make-firedata.py because DuckDB cannot read Arrow IPC over HTTP. The slider does not reach this panel: it has no cells to filter.

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
c AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin0_names[i] AS country FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
raw AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (p.day_idx) DAY AS dt, p.value AS v, c.country AS country
        FROM read_parquet('${firedata:raw}/${var:raw}_admin0.parquet') p
        JOIN c ON c.region_idx = p.region_idx),
-- El último día del registro, de TODO el fichero: un país sin fuego reciente no
-- puede decirnos hasta dónde llega el dato.
edge AS (SELECT CAST(strftime(max(dt),'%Y') AS INT) AS yr, CAST(strftime(max(dt),'%j') AS INT) AS doy FROM raw),
byday AS (SELECT CAST(strftime(dt,'%Y') AS INT) AS yr, CAST(strftime(dt,'%j') AS INT) AS doy, sum(v) AS v
          FROM raw WHERE ($country_sel = '' OR country = $country_sel) GROUP BY 1, 2),
years AS (SELECT DISTINCT CAST(strftime(dt,'%Y') AS INT) AS yr FROM raw),
-- Rejilla densa: sin ella la curva acumulada se rompe en cada día sin fuego.
grid AS (SELECT y.yr AS yr, g.doy AS doy
         FROM years y CROSS JOIN (SELECT unnest(range(1, 367)) AS doy) g CROSS JOIN edge e
         WHERE y.yr < e.yr OR (y.yr = e.yr AND g.doy <= e.doy)),
cum AS (SELECT g.yr AS yr, g.doy AS doy,
               sum(COALESCE(b.v, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY g.yr ORDER BY g.doy) / 1e9 AS c
        FROM grid g LEFT JOIN byday b ON b.yr = g.yr AND b.doy = g.doy),
-- Tres papeles, como el original: los años pasados en gris, su media, y el año
-- en curso. Etiquetarlos aquí evita overrides con el año escrito a mano.
series AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN cum.yr = e.yr THEN 'This year' ELSE cum.yr::VARCHAR END AS series,
         cum.doy AS doy, cum.c AS c
  FROM cum CROSS JOIN edge e
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Mean' AS series, cum.doy AS doy, avg(cum.c) AS c
  FROM cum CROSS JOIN edge e WHERE cum.yr < e.yr GROUP BY cum.doy)
PIVOT series ON series USING round(max(c), 4) GROUP BY doy ORDER BY doy

Magnitude and intensity are the contribution inside the selected country over the dashboard time range, as daily values; the anomaly σ is the whole-subdivision figure CAMS publishes for the $win window. targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1[i] AS adm1, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
areas AS (SELECT adm1, area_sq_km FROM read_parquet('https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/data/countries_admin1_v2gisco_z0.parquet')),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt, value, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])
       -- Slider threshold, same as the other aggregating panels.
       WHERE ($minval = '' OR value >= CAST($minval AS INTEGER))),
d AS (SELECT s.region_idx AS region_idx, s.adm1 AS adm1, s.name AS name, p.dt AS dt, sum(p.value) AS v
      FROM px p JOIN sub s ON s.region_idx = p.region_idx
                     JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
      WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt) AND ($country_sel = '' OR pa.country = $country_sel)
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4),
bounds AS (SELECT min(dt) AS d0, max(dt) AS d1 FROM d),
ndays AS (SELECT date_diff('day', d0, d1) + 1 AS n FROM bounds),
top AS (SELECT d.adm1 AS adm1, d.name AS name, sum(d.v) AS total
        FROM d JOIN areas a ON a.adm1 = d.adm1 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT ${topn:raw}),
sm AS (SELECT unnest(map_entries(windows['${win:raw}']['admin1'])) AS e
       FROM read_json('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/latest/${var:raw}/summary.json.gz',
         columns = {'dataset_day':'VARCHAR','variable':'VARCHAR',
                    'windows':'MAP(VARCHAR, MAP(VARCHAR, MAP(VARCHAR, DOUBLE[])))'})),
trend AS (SELECT d.adm1 AS adm1,
                 avg(CASE WHEN d.dt >  b.d1 - INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN d.v END) AS fin,
                 avg(CASE WHEN d.dt <  b.d0 + INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN d.v END) AS ini
          FROM d CROSS JOIN bounds b GROUP BY 1)
-- Rejilla densa región × día. El dato es disperso (una región sin fuego un día
-- no trae fila) y la conversión a series de Grafana necesita la rejilla completa:
-- sin esto el frame vuelve en formato largo y la sparkline no se dibuja.
, days AS (SELECT unnest(range(CAST((SELECT d0 FROM bounds) AS DATE),
                              CAST((SELECT d1 FROM bounds) AS DATE) + INTERVAL 1 DAY,
                              INTERVAL 1 DAY))::DATE AS dt)
SELECT g.dt AS "time", g.name AS region, -- sum() sobre INT32 da HUGEINT, que el driver entrega como string y
       -- deja el frame sin campo numérico: sin este cast no hay serie.
       CAST(COALESCE(d.v, 0) AS DOUBLE) AS value
FROM (SELECT top.adm1 AS adm1, top.name AS name, days.dt AS dt FROM top CROSS JOIN days) g
LEFT JOIN d ON d.adm1 = g.adm1 AND d.dt = g.dt
ORDER BY 1

WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1[i] AS adm1, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
areas AS (SELECT adm1, area_sq_km FROM read_parquet('https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/data/countries_admin1_v2gisco_z0.parquet')),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt, value, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])
       -- Slider threshold, same as the other aggregating panels.
       WHERE ($minval = '' OR value >= CAST($minval AS INTEGER))),
d AS (SELECT s.region_idx AS region_idx, s.adm1 AS adm1, s.name AS name, p.dt AS dt, sum(p.value) AS v
      FROM px p JOIN sub s ON s.region_idx = p.region_idx
                     JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
      WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt) AND ($country_sel = '' OR pa.country = $country_sel)
      GROUP BY 1,2,3,4),
bounds AS (SELECT min(dt) AS d0, max(dt) AS d1 FROM d),
ndays AS (SELECT date_diff('day', d0, d1) + 1 AS n FROM bounds),
top AS (SELECT d.adm1 AS adm1, d.name AS name, sum(d.v) AS total
        FROM d JOIN areas a ON a.adm1 = d.adm1 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT ${topn:raw}),
sm AS (SELECT unnest(map_entries(windows['${win:raw}']['admin1'])) AS e
       FROM read_json('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/latest/${var:raw}/summary.json.gz',
         columns = {'dataset_day':'VARCHAR','variable':'VARCHAR',
                    'windows':'MAP(VARCHAR, MAP(VARCHAR, MAP(VARCHAR, DOUBLE[])))'})),
trend AS (SELECT d.adm1 AS adm1,
                 avg(CASE WHEN d.dt >  b.d1 - INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN d.v END) AS fin,
                 avg(CASE WHEN d.dt <  b.d0 + INTERVAL 3 DAY THEN d.v END) AS ini
          FROM d CROSS JOIN bounds b GROUP BY 1)
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY top.total DESC) AS rank,
       top.name AS region,
       CASE WHEN t.fin IS NULL OR t.ini IS NULL OR t.ini = 0 THEN 0
            WHEN t.fin > t.ini * 1.05 THEN 1 WHEN t.fin < t.ini * 0.95 THEN -1 ELSE 0 END AS arrow,
       round(top.total / n.n / 1e3, 2) AS magnitude,
       round(top.total / n.n * CASE WHEN '${var:raw}' = 'cfire' THEN 1e3 ELSE 1e6 END / a.area_sq_km, 1) AS intensity,
       round(s.e.value[4], 2) AS anomaly
FROM top
CROSS JOIN ndays n
JOIN areas a ON a.adm1 = top.adm1
LEFT JOIN trend t ON t.adm1 = top.adm1
LEFT JOIN sm s ON s.e.key = top.adm1
ORDER BY top.total DESC

WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),

       round(sum(v) FILTER (WHERE CAST(strftime(dt,'%Y') AS INT) = (SELECT CAST(strftime(max(dt),'%Y') AS INT) FROM raw))/1e6, 3) AS "This year"

WHERE strftime(dt,'%m-%d') BETWEEN strftime(CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP),'%m-%d')

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1[i] AS adm1, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
              -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat, value, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])),
pick AS (SELECT s.adm1 AS adm1, s.region_idx AS region_idx, s.iso3 AS iso3
         FROM sub s JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
         WHERE $region_sel <> '' AND s.name = $region_sel
           AND ($country_sel = '' OR pa.country = $country_sel))
-- sum() sobre INT32 da HUGEINT, que el driver entrega como texto: sin el CAST
-- el mapa recibe `value` como cadena y ni la rampa de color ni el filtro de
-- rango del slider enganchan.
SELECT ST_AsHEXWKB(ST_MakeEnvelope(p.lon-0.05, p.lat-0.05, p.lon+0.05, p.lat+0.05)) AS geom,
       round(CAST(sum(p.value) AS DOUBLE), 1) AS value,
       count(*) AS ndays
FROM px p JOIN pick ON pick.region_idx = p.region_idx
WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt)
GROUP BY p.lon, p.lat

WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1[i] AS adm1, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
              -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat, value, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])),
pick AS (SELECT s.adm1 AS adm1, s.region_idx AS region_idx, s.iso3 AS iso3
         FROM sub s JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
         WHERE $region_sel <> '' AND s.name = $region_sel
           AND ($country_sel = '' OR pa.country = $country_sel)),
-- El total de la subdivisión, para que la capa tenga con qué colorearse. Llega
-- a kepler como `count`: el plugin da el papel `count` a una columna llamada
-- `total` y la renombra.
tot AS (SELECT CAST(sum(p.value) AS DOUBLE) AS total
        FROM px p JOIN pick ON pick.region_idx = p.region_idx
        WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt))
SELECT ST_AsHEXWKB(ST_CollectionExtract(ST_MakeValid(ST_GeomFromText(
         'MULTIPOLYGON(' || list_aggregate(list_transform(g.geometry, poly ->
             '(' || list_aggregate(list_transform(poly, ring ->
                 '(' || list_aggregate(list_transform(
                     CASE WHEN ring[1] = ring[len(ring)] THEN ring ELSE list_append(ring, ring[1]) END,
                     pt -> pt[1]::VARCHAR || ' ' || pt[2]::VARCHAR), 'string_agg', ', ') || ')'
             ), 'string_agg', ', ') || ')'
         ), 'string_agg', ', ') || ')')), 3)) AS geom,
       g.name AS subdivision,
       round(COALESCE((SELECT total FROM tot), 0) / 1e3, 2) AS total
FROM read_parquet('https://apps.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/fire-emissions-watch/data/countries_admin1_v2gisco.parquet') g JOIN pick ON pick.adm1 = g.adm1

panels.description: Every year since 2003 for the selected subdivision, its climatological mean, and the year in progress. Read from the converted admin1 series.

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
pick AS (SELECT s.region_idx AS region_idx
         FROM sub s JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
         WHERE $region_sel <> '' AND s.name = $region_sel
           AND ($country_sel = '' OR pa.country = $country_sel)),
raw AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (p.day_idx) DAY AS dt, p.value AS v, p.region_idx AS ridx
        FROM read_parquet('${firedata:raw}/${var:raw}_admin1.parquet') p),
mine AS (SELECT r.dt AS dt, r.v AS v FROM raw r JOIN pick ON pick.region_idx = r.ridx)
, edge AS (SELECT CAST(strftime(max(dt),'%Y') AS INT) AS yr, CAST(strftime(max(dt),'%j') AS INT) AS doy FROM raw),
byday AS (SELECT CAST(strftime(dt,'%Y') AS INT) AS yr, CAST(strftime(dt,'%j') AS INT) AS doy, sum(v) AS v
          FROM mine GROUP BY 1, 2),
years AS (SELECT DISTINCT CAST(strftime(dt,'%Y') AS INT) AS yr FROM raw),
grid AS (SELECT y.yr AS yr, g.doy AS doy
         FROM years y CROSS JOIN (SELECT unnest(range(1, 367)) AS doy) g CROSS JOIN edge e
         -- Sin región elegida la rejilla queda vacía, y el panel enseña nada
         -- en vez de veinticuatro líneas planas de cero.
         WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pick)
           AND (y.yr < e.yr OR (y.yr = e.yr AND g.doy <= e.doy))),
cum AS (SELECT g.yr AS yr, g.doy AS doy,
               sum(COALESCE(b.v, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY g.yr ORDER BY g.doy) / 1e6 AS c
        FROM grid g LEFT JOIN byday b ON b.yr = g.yr AND b.doy = g.doy),
series AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN cum.yr = e.yr THEN 'This year' ELSE cum.yr::VARCHAR END AS series, cum.doy AS doy, cum.c AS c
  FROM cum CROSS JOIN edge e
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Mean', cum.doy, avg(cum.c) FROM cum CROSS JOIN edge e WHERE cum.yr < e.yr GROUP BY cum.doy)
PIVOT series ON series USING round(max(c), 5) GROUP BY doy ORDER BY doy

panels.title: Daily playback

panels.description: Cells aggregated to 0.5° — at 0.1° the columns render as hairs — with height proportional to the square root of the value, one polygon per cell per day. Shares its clock with the map on the left, and flies to whatever point you click on the map above. At rest it shows each cell's peak day, because the days overlap and the tallest one wins. Flat basemap on purpose: deck.gl does not drape data over terrain, so over a relief basemap the low cells would be buried inside the mountains.

targets.rawSql:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
reg AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
countries AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country, admin0_continent[i] AS continente
        FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
                     -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat,
                     lon_idx, lat_idx, value, region_idx
              FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}])),
agr AS (
  SELECT (p.lon_idx // 5) AS gx, (p.lat_idx // 5) AS gy, p.dt AS dt,
         sum(p.value) AS value, any_value(c.country) AS country
  FROM px p
  LEFT JOIN reg r ON r.region_idx = p.region_idx
  LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.iso3 = r.iso3
  WHERE $__timeFilter(p.dt)
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3)
SELECT ST_AsHEXWKB(ST_MakeEnvelope(-180.0 + gx*0.5, -90.0 + gy*0.5,
                                   -179.5 + gx*0.5, -89.5 + gy*0.5)) AS geom,
       dt AS "time",
       round(CAST(value AS DOUBLE), 1) AS value,
       country
FROM agr

list.name: cLat
list.query:
WITH idx AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
reg AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3 FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country FROM idx, range(1, len(idx.admin0)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
              -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat, value, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}]))
-- Centre of the country's fire activity, not of its bounding box: box
-- centroids send Ecuador to the Galapagos and Russia to the prime meridian.
-- Empty when no country is picked, which leaves the map where it is.
SELECT CAST(round(avg(p.lat), 4) AS VARCHAR) AS __text,
       CAST(round(avg(p.lat), 4) AS VARCHAR) AS __value
FROM px p
JOIN reg r ON r.region_idx = p.region_idx
JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = r.iso3
-- Explicit range: the time-filter macro does not expand in a variable
-- query, and naming it even inside a comment breaks macro expansion,
-- which is textual and does not respect SQL comments.
WHERE p.dt BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP) AND ${country_sel:sqlstring} <> '' AND pa.country = ${country_sel:sqlstring}

list.label: Subdivision
list.name: region_sel
list.query:
WITH j AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin0)+1) t(i))
-- A variable query is not quoted the way a panel query is, so the country goes
-- through the sqlstring formatter, which also escapes names like Cote d'Ivoire.
SELECT __text, __value FROM (
  SELECT 0 AS ord, 'All subdivisions' AS __text, '' AS __value
  UNION ALL
  -- Only the subdivisions of the chosen country. Listing all 4 620 would be
  -- unusable, and their names are not unique across countries — two Santa
  -- Cruzes would resolve to both at once.
  SELECT DISTINCT 1, s.name, s.name
  FROM sub s JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
  WHERE ${country_sel:sqlstring} <> '' AND pa.country = ${country_sel:sqlstring})
ORDER BY ord, __text

list.query:
WITH j AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin0)+1) t(i)),
subidx AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
           FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin1)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
              -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}]))
-- Centre of the subdivision's own fire activity. Explicit range: the
-- time-filter macro does not expand in a variable query, and naming it even in
-- a comment breaks expansion, which is textual.
SELECT CAST(round(avg(p.lat), 4) AS VARCHAR) AS __text,
       CAST(round(avg(p.lat), 4) AS VARCHAR) AS __value
FROM px p
JOIN subidx s ON s.region_idx = p.region_idx
JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
WHERE p.dt BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP)

list.name: rLng
list.query:
WITH j AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('https://sites.ecmwf.int/data/cams/products/gfas/v2_gisco_fp/regions/region_index.json')),
sub AS (SELECT admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
        FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin1)+1) t(i)),
parent AS (SELECT admin0[i] AS iso3, admin0_names[i] AS country
           FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin0)+1) t(i)),
subidx AS (SELECT i-1 AS region_idx, admin1_names[i] AS name, admin1_parent[i] AS iso3
           FROM j, range(1, len(j.admin1)+1) t(i)),
px AS (SELECT DATE '2003-01-01' + INTERVAL (day_idx) DAY AS dt,
              -179.95 + lon_idx*0.1 AS lon, -89.95 + lat_idx*0.1 AS lat, region_idx
       FROM read_parquet([${months:sqlstring}]))
-- Centre of the subdivision's own fire activity. Explicit range: the
-- time-filter macro does not expand in a variable query, and naming it even in
-- a comment breaks expansion, which is textual.
SELECT CAST(round(avg(p.lon), 4) AS VARCHAR) AS __text,
       CAST(round(avg(p.lon), 4) AS VARCHAR) AS __value
FROM px p
JOIN subidx s ON s.region_idx = p.region_idx
JOIN parent pa ON pa.iso3 = s.iso3
WHERE p.dt BETWEEN CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP) AND CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP)
  AND ${region_sel:sqlstring} <> '' AND s.name = ${region_sel:sqlstring}
  AND (${country_sel:sqlstring} = '' OR pa.country = ${country_sel:sqlstring})
